title: Jack Lucas — the 14-year-old who threw himself on two grenades
sources: Wikipedia: Jacklyn H. 'Jack' Lucas (14 February 1928 – 5 June 2008) — enlisted in the Marine Corps Reserve on 8 August 1942 aged 14, forging his mother's signature on the consent form, claiming to be 17 and bribing a notary; he was 5 ft 8 and 180 lb; in January 1945 he walked out of camp at Pearl Harbor and stowed away on USS Deuel, carrying Marines to Iwo Jima; on 8 February, the day before he would have been listed as a deserter, he turned himself in and was assigned as a rifleman, reduced in rank to private; he turned 17 at sea on 14 February; landed on Iwo Jima on 19 February; on 20 February, in a trench with three Marines, two Japanese grenades landed among them; he jammed one into the volcanic ash with his rifle and covered it with his body, and pulled the other beneath him; one exploded, the other did not; his three comrades were unharmed and left, believing him dead; Marines from another unit found him and called corpsmen; he underwent 21 surgeries and carried about 200 pieces of metal in his body for life, which set off airport metal detectors; President Truman presented the Medal of Honor on 5 October 1945; youngest Marine and youngest serviceman of WWII to receive it; in 1961 he joined the Army as a paratrooper to conquer his fear of heights and reportedly survived a training jump in which both parachutes malfunctioned; died 2008; the destroyer USS Jack H. Lucas was commissioned in 2023

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / US Marine Corps / US Navy / Library of Congress): PFC Jack Lucas with the Medal of Honor; Marines training at Parris Island; the Iwo Jima landings, February 1945; Mount Suribachi; Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima (Joe Rosenthal); Lucas's funeral, 2008 (USMC)

Archive film (public domain): 'To the Shores of Iwo Jima' (US Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard, 1945, colour); Marines evacuated from Iwo Jima, February 1945; the flag raising on Mount Suribachi (colour) — illustrative, not Lucas himself
Music: Marines' Hymn (slow) — United States Marine Band, public domain

post.facebook:
Two grenades landed in the trench. A 17-year-old Marine threw himself on both of them.

Jack Lucas had been lying about his age since he was fourteen. In 1942 he forged his mother's signature, bribed a notary and joined the Marines. They kept him far from the fighting, in Hawaii — so he stowed away on a ship heading for Iwo Jima. He turned himself in at sea, one day before he'd have been listed as a deserter, and they handed him a rifle. He turned 17 on the way.

On his second day on Iwo Jima, he and three Marines dived into a trench under fire. Two grenades landed at their feet. Lucas shoved one into the volcanic ash, covered it with his body, and pulled the other under him. One exploded; the other never went off. His three friends walked away without a scratch — they thought he was dead.

He wasn't. It took 21 operations, and about 200 pieces of metal stayed in his body for life, setting off airport metal detectors. In October 1945 President Truman gave him the Medal of Honor — the youngest Marine to receive it in the war. Years later he became an Army paratrooper; on one jump, both his parachutes reportedly failed. He survived that too.

💥 #History #WW2 #IwoJima #Marines
